blog_items.title: 10 Essential Tips for Creating Engaging Social Media Videos
blog_items.excerpt: Learn the secrets to creating scroll-stopping social media content that captures attention and drives engagement.
blog_items.author: Victoria Opemipo
blog_items.content:
"Learn the secrets to creating scroll-stopping social media content that captures attention and drives engagement."

Social media video is the most competitive creative arena in existence. You have less than two seconds to prevent a thumb from scrolling past your content. That's not hyperbole — it's the documented average attention threshold before a decision to scroll is made.

1. Lead With the Payoff

Traditional storytelling builds to a climax. Social video inverts this. Your most compelling moment — the reveal, the transformation, the surprising fact — goes in the first three seconds. This is called a hook-first structure and it consistently outperforms slow-burn openings by 3–5x in completion rate.

2. Design for Silent Viewing

Over 70% of social video is watched without sound. If your video only works with audio, it's likely missing a large portion of your audience. Use bold on-screen text, expressive visuals, and clear visual storytelling.

If you can't communicate your message in silent mode, your video isn't working hard enough. — Michael Chen, Creative Director

3. Match Energy to Platform

  • TikTok: Raw, fast, trend-aware, under 30 seconds
  • Instagram Reels: Polished but personal, 15–30 seconds
  • YouTube Shorts: Educational or entertaining, up to 60 seconds
  • LinkedIn: Authority-driven, measured, 60–90 seconds

job_openings.title: Senior Video Producer
job_openings.overview: Lead end-to-end commercial video productions from concept through final delivery. You will manage shoots, direct talent, and collaborate with editors and strategists to deliver premium content for top-tier brands.
job_openings.responsibilities:
• Lead and manage 8-12 video productions per month across commercial, brand, and social formats
  • Develop creative treatments, shot lists, and production schedules
  • Direct on-set talent, crew, and client stakeholders
  • Collaborate with post-production team on rough cuts, revisions, and final delivery
  • Manage production budgets and vendor relationships
  • Mentor junior producers and interns

Requirements
  • 5+ years of professional video production experience in commercial or agency setting
  • Proficiency with professional cinema cameras (RED, Sony FX, Canon C-series)
  • Strong understanding of lighting, composition, and visual storytelling
  • Experience managing shoots with 5+ crew members
  • Excellent client communication and presentation skills
  • Portfolio demonstrating 10+ completed commercial projects

Nice to Have
  • Experience with live streaming production
  • FAA Part 107 drone license
  • Adobe Premiere / DaVinci Resolve proficiency
  • Bilingual (Spanish) preferred

Benefits
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with 4% company match
  • Unlimited PTO (minimum 15 days encouraged)
  • Annual equipment stipend ($2,500)
  • Professional development budget ($3,000/year)
  • Flexible hybrid schedule (3 days in studio, 2 remote)
